label: conj:atom-braid-exterior-algebra
title: Canonical atom-braid `atom_braid_word_3A(Z, N)` in `H_{3A}(q)` generates a sub-algebra graded-isomorphic to the exterior algebra Λ*(ℂ^{3A−Z}) with grade shift δ = Z−1; total dim = 2^{3A−Z}, k-th component dim = C(3A−Z, k−δ). Empirically verified across D, T, ³He, ⁴He.
html:
Conjecture. Canonical atom-braid atom_braid_word_3A(Z, N) in H_{3A}(q) generates a sub-algebra graded-isomorphic to the exterior algebra Λ(ℂ^{3A−Z}) with grade shift δ = Z−1; total dim = 2^{3A−Z}, k-th component dim = C(3A−Z, k−δ). Empirically verified across D, T, ³He, ⁴He.*

Conjecture (atom-braid exterior-algebra structure). Let T_w(Z, N) \in H_{3A}(q) denote the canonical atomic Hecke word. It generates a sub-algebra whose Gröbner-Shirshov normal-form filtration shape is given by:

  \dim_R \bigl(F_k(T_w(Z, N))\bigr) \;=\; \binom{3A - Z}{k - (Z - 1)}.

The sub-algebra is isomorphic to the exterior algebra \Lambda^*(R^{3A - Z}) with grade shift \delta = Z - 1.

The canonical atom-braid populates a fermion Fock-space subalgebra of H_{3A}(q). Each interface between adjacent strands contributes one binary degree of freedom. The proton count Z enforces dimension reduction (removing one degree of freedom per proton) and a grade shift (offsetting the filtration bound).

This exterior structure restricts the active dimension. For ^4\mathrm{He}, the dimension collapses from the 12! standard Wedderburn basis to exactly 2^{10} = 1024. The restriction governs the computational complexity of the canonical solver.
